Injection 4 fully resolved every pair with substantial margin; shortening only its gradient tests how much of that margin can be traded for speed. Keeping the low starting organic fraction protects the early peaks while targeting last-peak elution near 10 minutes.

Lengthen the best gradient by one step to improve the sole under-resolved pair, which responded strongly to a shallower gradient in injection 4. The last peak should remain near 10 minutes, giving a strong chance of reaching or closely approaching CRF 1.0.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to bring the last peak clearly below 10 minutes while slightly flattening the gradient. The early pair has ample resolution margin, and the shallower slope may preserve full resolution of the critical middle pair.

Raise temperature one step while holding the gradient fixed to test whether a shorter run can retain full resolution. This isolates temperature selectivity at the critical middle pair, with injection 11 preserved as the maximum-score fallback.

Test whether higher temperature carries the critical pair through an elution-order reversal and restores separation while shortening retention. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate this selectivity change; injection 11 remains the maximum-score fallback.

Lengthen injection 13’s gradient one step to try to lift the new critical pair from R 1.41 above 1.5 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Monitor the other close pair at R 1.74, since its separation may respond differently to the shallower slope.

Use a gradient slope between injections 13 and 14 by reducing the endpoint to 0.80 at 14 minutes. This should preserve full resolution of both critical pairs while shortening last-peak retention relative to injection 14.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten the fastest fully resolved method while slightly flattening its gradient. Check whether the early pair and the critical middle pairs retain R ≥ 1.5; injection 15 remains the faster maximum-score fallback.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the pair that deteriorated sharply in injection 16, and use a steeper gradient to shorten the run. This tests whether the selectivity advantage of the lower start permits full resolution faster than injection 15.

Shorten the fastest fully resolved gradient by one step to test the speed limit at this temperature and starting composition. Monitor both close middle pairs; injection 17 remains the fully resolved fallback if either drops below R 1.5.

Use a slope between injections 17 and 18 to target R just above 1.5 for the limiting pair while shortening last-peak retention relative to injection 17. The 0.75 endpoint remains above the observed elution window, so all peaks should still elute during the gradient.

Test whether a lower starting organic fraction restores the limiting pair’s resolution in the faster 10-minute gradient from injection 18. This may beat injection 19’s elution time, but the other close middle pair must also remain above R 1.5.

Slightly flatten injection 20’s gradient to lift the limiting pair above R 1.5, targeting full resolution with last-peak elution around 7.6 minutes. The other close pair has little margin, so its resolution will determine whether this improves on injection 19.

Raise temperature one grid step while keeping injection 21’s gradient fixed to test for a faster fully resolved method. Both close middle pairs require monitoring for selectivity changes; injection 21 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction and steeper gradient move the coalescing middle pair through an elution-order reversal at 60 C, potentially restoring resolution in a much shorter run. Injection 21 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Test a steeper gradient to increase separation of the middle pair after its apparent elution-order reversal, targeting a substantially faster fully resolved method. Monitor the neighboring pair at R 2.12 for compression; injection 21 remains the fastest proven maximum-score fallback.

Return to the successful 55 C region and slightly flatten injection 17’s gradient to seek more balanced resolution margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 21 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method; this final run targets a more robust maximum-score alternative.
